posts.text: A lyrebird can reproduce a chainsaw, a car alarm, a camera shutter, and a human voice. One has been recorded doing an entire construction site.
comments: It is not approximating the sound. It is reproducing it well enough that people look around for the machine.
Send it to whoever thinks parrots are the impressive mimics → https://beastlyfacts.com/facts/natures-sound-thief/

posts.text: Ferrets are moderately priced to buy and expensive to keep, and almost none of that is day-to-day care. It is a near-inevitable pattern of costly age-related illness.
comments: A rescue ferret is $50 to $150 and often already altered and vet checked. That is the last cheap number in the timeline → https://beastlyfacts.com/blog/ferret-cost-guide/

posts.text: The blobfish only looks like that on land. At the depth it actually lives, pressure holds it in shape as a fairly normal fish with a big nose.
comments: It got voted the world's ugliest animal based entirely on a photo of it dying from decompression.
One for anyone who has only seen the meme → https://beastlyfacts.com/facts/underwater-makeover/

posts.text: Polar bear skin is black and the fur is transparent. It only looks white because it reflects visible light, the same way snow does.
comments: The black skin underneath is doing the heat absorption.
Good one for a kid who likes being told the obvious thing is wrong → https://beastlyfacts.com/facts/black-skin-clear-fur/

posts.text: Goldfish are hardier than their reputation when they are kept properly. Start with the water: any ammonia or nitrite reading above 0 is urgent, and most outbreaks start right there.
comments: Ich is the classic, white spots like grains of salt plus flashing against the decor, and it tracks stress and water quality closely → https://beastlyfacts.com/blog/goldfish-health-issues-guide/

posts.text: Nine-banded armadillos always give birth to four identical babies, from a single egg that splits.
comments: Natural clones, every litter, every time.
Send it to anyone who thinks twins are unusual → https://beastlyfacts.com/facts/identical-quadruplets/

posts.text: A pufferfish can inflate to three times its size, and it also carries a toxin 1,200 times deadlier than cyanide.
comments: The inflating is the part everyone knows. The toxin is the part that matters.
For the person who orders fugu to seem brave → https://beastlyfacts.com/facts/balloon-defense/

posts.text: The first real decision with sugar gliders is not financial, it is legal, and it needs settling before a single dollar gets budgeted.
comments: Illegal statewide in California, Alaska and Hawaii, effectively illegal in Pennsylvania, banned in DC and New York City, permit required in New Jersey → https://beastlyfacts.com/blog/sugar-glider-cost-guide/

posts.text: A single starfish arm can regenerate a whole new body. Some species split themselves in half and become two.
comments: Which makes cutting one up a spectacularly bad way to get rid of it.
Send it to whoever thinks starfish are simple → https://beastlyfacts.com/facts/arm-regeneration-masters/

posts.text: Alpacas spit when annoyed, threatened, or competing for food, and it travels up to 10 feet.
comments: It is their main defense. The fluffy exterior is doing a lot of public relations work.
For anyone planning an alpaca farm visit → https://beastlyfacts.com/facts/spit-happens/

posts.text: Box turtles hide illness well, and several of their common conditions connect to each other, which makes knowing the warning signs unusually worthwhile here.
comments: A misshapen shell, deformed legs and stunted growth all point the same way: calcium and phosphorus imbalance, inadequate UVB, or poor diet → https://beastlyfacts.com/blog/box-turtle-health-issues-guide/

posts.text: Capybaras are so relaxed that birds, monkeys, and even caimans will sit on them.
comments: Largest rodent in the world, and apparently furniture.
Send it to the person who wants one → https://beastlyfacts.com/facts/the-chillest-animal/

posts.text: Sharks have jelly-filled pores that detect the electrical field of another animal's heartbeat, from over a meter away.
comments: They are called ampullae of Lorenzini. Hiding from a shark means hiding your pulse.
For whoever thinks staying still helps → https://beastlyfacts.com/facts/electric-sense/

posts.text: Canaries are one of the more affordable pet birds, right up until you get into the song and show breeds, where the number climbs fast.
comments: Common yellows run $25 to $60. Red Factors, bred for color, $80 to $150. Specialized song breeds go higher again → https://beastlyfacts.com/blog/canary-cost-guide/

posts.text: Goats develop regional accents. Kids raised in different social groups end up with distinct bleats.
comments: Scientists treat it as evidence of social learning in a species previously assumed to have fixed vocalizations.
Send it to someone who underestimates goats → https://beastlyfacts.com/facts/regional-accents/

posts.text: Every zebra's stripe pattern is unique, and a foal learns its mother's pattern within hours of being born.
comments: It recognizes her by stripes alone. That is the whole identification system.
One for anyone who says they all look the same → https://beastlyfacts.com/facts/no-two-stripes-alike/

posts.text: Many areas have no vet who treats invertebrates at all. With a tarantula, correct husbandry is not most of the care, it is nearly all of it.
comments: Dehydration is the common one: shriveled wrinkled abdomen, lethargy, and the legs curling in tight underneath, the death curl → https://beastlyfacts.com/blog/tarantula-health-issues-guide/

posts.text: Honey badgers are nearly immune to snake venom. Filmed getting bitten by a cobra, going limp for a few minutes, then waking up and finishing the snake.
comments: Not surviving the bite. Napping through it and resuming the meal.
Send this to whoever still doubts the reputation → https://beastlyfacts.com/facts/snake-venom-no-thanks/

posts.text: Mantis shrimp have 16 types of color receptor. You have 3. They also see ultraviolet and polarized light, and punch with the force of a bullet.
comments: Sixteen receptors and a weapon. It is an unreasonable animal.
For the friend who is proud of their color vision → https://beastlyfacts.com/facts/mantis-shrimp-vision/

posts.text: Green iguana health problems trace back overwhelmingly to husbandry, and one condition is common enough that it should shape every other decision about care.
comments: VCA Animal Hospitals describes metabolic bone disease as probably the most common medical problem in captive iguanas → https://beastlyfacts.com/blog/green-iguana-health-issues-guide/

posts.text: Elephants hold funerals. They touch the bones of dead family members with their trunks and stand vigil for hours.
comments: They have been seen crying doing it.
Send it to anyone who thinks grief is a human thing → https://beastlyfacts.com/facts/elephants-mourn/

posts.text: Crows recognize individual human faces for years, and they teach other crows who counts as friend or foe.
comments: The ones who like you sometimes bring gifts. Buttons, earrings, whatever they found.
Send it to the person feeding crows in their yard → https://beastlyfacts.com/facts/crow-detectives/

posts.text: Axolotls are hardy in the right conditions and surprisingly fragile outside them, and a large share of what goes wrong traces back to water that is too warm.
comments: Fungal infection reads as white or grey cotton-like growth on the gills or body, usually triggered by warm water, poor quality, stress, or an injury → https://beastlyfacts.com/blog/axolotl-health-issues-guide/

posts.text: The Turritopsis dohrnii jellyfish is biologically immortal. Old or stressed, it reverts its cells to a younger state and starts over.
comments: An actual reset button on aging, running in the ocean right now.
For whoever wants the real version of immortality → https://beastlyfacts.com/facts/immortal-jellyfish/

posts.text: Sea otters hold hands while sleeping so they do not drift apart. They also wrap up in kelp for the same reason.
comments: A group of them floating together is called a raft, which is almost too on the nose.
Send it to someone having a rough day → https://beastlyfacts.com/facts/sea-otter-hand-holding/

posts.text: Cockatiels are affordable to buy, and the real budgeting story is how long you will be doing it. A 10 to 15 year lifespan makes this a long-term commitment at a low entry price.
comments: The cage is frequently the single biggest line item in the setup, often more than the bird itself → https://beastlyfacts.com/blog/cockatiel-cost-guide/

posts.text: Tardigrades survive space, temperatures from -328F to 300F, and being fully dried out for decades.
comments: Half a millimeter long, and functionally unkillable.
For anyone who thinks cockroaches are the survivors → https://beastlyfacts.com/facts/indestructible-water-bears/

posts.text: A ball python can go months without eating during breeding season, and that is completely normal.
comments: It is natural fasting, not illness. Which is the thing new keepers panic about most.
Send it to whoever is worried about theirs right now → https://beastlyfacts.com/facts/months-without-eating/

posts.text: Hamsters are hardy for their size, but a short lifespan means things progress fast, so recognizing the warning signs matters more here than with most pets.
comments: Wet tail is the one to know on sight. A large veterinary study found it both the most commonly diagnosed condition and the leading specific cause of death → https://beastlyfacts.com/blog/hamster-health-issues-guide/

posts.text: Crested geckos were considered extinct until someone found them again in New Caledonia in 1994.
comments: Thirty years later they are one of the most common geckos in the hobby.
For anyone who assumes extinct is final → https://beastlyfacts.com/facts/rediscovered-in-1994/

posts.text: Chameleons do not mainly change color to hide. They do it to communicate mood and temperature.
comments: Stress, excitement, readiness to mate. The camouflage explanation is the one that stuck anyway.
Send it to whoever bought one to watch it match things → https://beastlyfacts.com/facts/color-means-communication/

posts.text: Neon tetras are among the cheapest fish you can keep, and unlike a betta, the cost planning starts from the fact that you are buying several at once.
comments: Most run $1 to $3 each. It is a schooling species, so you are buying a group of 6 to 12, not a fish → https://beastlyfacts.com/blog/neon-tetra-cost-guide/

posts.text: Guinea pigs are highly social and should be kept in pairs or small groups. A lone one can become anxious and genuinely depressed.
comments: One guinea pig is not a smaller commitment. It is a worse one.
For anyone about to buy a single pig → https://beastlyfacts.com/facts/guinea-pigs-are-social/

posts.text: Tortoises routinely live past 100, which means adopting one can mean naming it in your will.
comments: That is not a joke about commitment. People actually have to do it.
Send it to someone who thinks a dog is a long commitment → https://beastlyfacts.com/facts/100-year-commitment/

posts.text: Blue-tongued skink is really two pets wearing one name, and nowhere is that clearer than on the price tag. Where yours comes from changes almost every number.
comments: Northern Australian skinks run $150 for babies to $250 for adults, high-color morphs $400 to $700. Indonesian skinks are noticeably cheaper → https://beastlyfacts.com/blog/blue-tongue-skink-cost-guide/

posts.text: Wolves returning to Yellowstone in 1995 changed elk behavior and let some vegetation recover. That part is real and it has a name, a trophic cascade.
comments: The version where wolves reshaped the rivers single-handedly has been challenged. The truth is smaller and still remarkable.
For anyone who has shared the viral video → https://beastlyfacts.com/facts/the-river-story-revisited/

posts.text: Some tamarin monkeys communicate through tail movements, carrying real messages across the troop.
comments: A social network run largely on tail position.
Send it to whoever thinks small primates are simple → https://beastlyfacts.com/facts/mission-impossible-tails/

posts.text: Nearly everything on the savannah monitor health list traces back to one root cause, more than in almost any other pet reptile: a mismatch between how much it gets fed and how much it would actually burn.
comments: In the wild they eat a lean, largely insect-based diet on a seasonal cycle. Captivity rarely reproduces either half of that → https://beastlyfacts.com/blog/savannah-monitor-health-issues-guide/

posts.text: Cuttlefish change color and texture in a blink, using skin cells called chromatophores.
comments: Camouflage is only half of it. The other half is performance.
For anyone who has never watched one do it → https://beastlyfacts.com/facts/underwater-fireworks/

posts.text: Red-footed boobies dive from up to 30 feet into the ocean and can see clearly underwater once they get there.
comments: The eye structure handles both, which most diving birds cannot manage.
Send it to someone who only knows the name → https://beastlyfacts.com/facts/invisible-wings/

posts.text: Almost every common betta illness traces back to water quality or water temperature, which is genuinely good news, because it means the first move is always the same.
comments: Fin rot is the frequent one: frayed, ragged or discolored fins, treated with clean water and aquarium salt before anything stronger → https://beastlyfacts.com/blog/betta-fish-health-issues-guide/

posts.text: A kookaburra's call sounds like genuine human laughter, and it is territorial, not cheerful.
comments: You hear it echoing across the Australian outback at sunrise. It is a warning.
For whoever finds the sound charming → https://beastlyfacts.com/facts/rollercoaster-tails/

posts.text: Geckos run across ceilings using microscopic hairs on their feet and van der Waals forces.
comments: Molecular attraction, holding up an entire animal, upside down.
Send it to someone who thinks it is suction → https://beastlyfacts.com/facts/climbing-the-walls/

posts.text: Before anything else with rabbits: they need a rabbit-savvy exotic vet, not a standard small-animal clinic, and you want that found before you need it.
comments: GI stasis is the one to understand. The gut slows or stops, gas builds, and it is genuinely life-threatening if it is not caught quickly → https://beastlyfacts.com/blog/rabbit-health-issues-guide/

posts.text: Ronan the California sea lion is the first nonhuman mammal proven to keep a precise beat, and she often matches or beats human consistency.
comments: Including on rhythms she has never heard before.
For anyone who says animals have no sense of rhythm → https://beastlyfacts.com/facts/rhythm-keeping-sea-lion/

posts.text: Wallace's flying frog does not just leap. It steers, using enormous webbed feet as parachutes and rudders.
comments: Mid-air course correction, then a controlled landing on a distant branch.
Send it to whoever likes an unlikely aerodynamic story → https://beastlyfacts.com/facts/gliding-rainforest-acrobat/

posts.text: Hermit crabs get sold as an impulse buy at beach shops, which is exactly the wrong way to think about them. Done properly they need a real setup.
comments: The crabs themselves are usually the smallest line item, and you need at least two, because they do badly alone → https://beastlyfacts.com/blog/hermit-crab-cost-guide/

posts.text: In breeding season male hairy frogs grow temporary hair, actually fringes of skin packed with blood vessels.
comments: It absorbs extra oxygen while they guard eggs in fast, low-oxygen water. Dad grows gills on his legs.
For the friend who likes body horror with a happy ending → https://beastlyfacts.com/facts/hairy-oxygen-boosting-dads/

posts.text: Male gentoo and Adelie penguins pick out the perfect smooth pebble and present it to a female. If she accepts, it goes into the nest.
comments: A well chosen pebble can start a lifelong pair bond.
Send it to whoever is overthinking a gift → https://beastlyfacts.com/facts/pebble-proposing-love-birds/

posts.text: Chinchillas hide illness well and can decline quickly once something is wrong, which makes the warning signs, and one specific environmental risk, worth knowing in advance.
comments: Dental disease is the most common chronic issue. Teeth grow continuously, and without enough coarse hay to grind them down, spikes or impacted roots develop → https://beastlyfacts.com/blog/chinchilla-health-issues-guide/

posts.text: Woodpeckers peck 20 times a second and never concuss. Not because the skull cushions the blow, a 2022 study killed that idea.
comments: The skull stays rigid so they hammer harder. They survive it because a tiny brain takes a tiny hit.
For anyone who learned the shock absorber version → https://beastlyfacts.com/facts/small-brain-zero-concussions/

posts.text: In some anglerfish species the male fuses permanently to the female, skin and blood vessels merging, until he is little more than a built-in sperm supply.
comments: He was a fraction of her size to begin with.
Send it to someone who thinks their relationship is codependent → https://beastlyfacts.com/facts/the-ultimate-clingy-partner/

posts.text: Russian tortoises are hardy, and most of what goes wrong comes back to three husbandry basics that sit entirely within an owner's control: temperature, humidity, diet.
comments: VCA lists metabolic bone disease among the most common conditions in pet tortoises. Soft or deformed shell, weak limbs, from inadequate UVB or dietary calcium → https://beastlyfacts.com/blog/russian-tortoise-health-issues-guide/

posts.text: A giant squid's eye runs up to 27 cm across, roughly a dinner plate. Largest eyes in the animal kingdom.
comments: Built to catch the faintest bioluminescent flicker, thousands of feet down.
For whoever likes deep sea scale → https://beastlyfacts.com/facts/dinner-plate-eyes/

posts.text: An alligator bites at nearly 3,000 pounds of force, and the muscles that open its jaw are weak enough that a person can hold it shut by hand.
comments: All the power is in one direction. None of it is in the other.
Send it to the person who quotes bite force stats → https://beastlyfacts.com/facts/all-bite-no-bark/

posts.text: Boa constrictors are affordable at the entry level, and most of what gets sold as a boa is one specific type worth understanding before you buy.
comments: It affects both the price and what you are actually getting. Legality is mostly a non-issue, with a couple of states worth checking → https://beastlyfacts.com/blog/boa-constrictor-cost-guide/

posts.text: The star-nosed mole's 22 nose tentacles carry over 25,000 sensory receptors, and it identifies and eats food in about 120 milliseconds.
comments: Fastest eating speed recorded in any mammal.
For anyone who eats too fast → https://beastlyfacts.com/facts/fastest-eater-alive/

posts.text: The basenji cannot bark. Its larynx is shaped wrong, so it yodels instead, a sound owners call the baroo.
comments: Barkless on paper. Nobody who lives with one calls them quiet.
Send it to whoever wants a silent dog → https://beastlyfacts.com/facts/the-dog-that-doesnt-bark/

posts.text: Lovebirds are one of the more affordable parrots, and the name promises something gentler than what you get. This is a small bird with a real capacity for territorial behavior.
comments: Common peach-faced or Fischer's run $50 to $150. Rare mutations $200 to $400 or more, with exceptional individuals reaching $1,000 → https://beastlyfacts.com/blog/lovebird-cost-guide/

posts.text: Koalas have fingerprints so close to human ones that forensic experts have struggled to tell them apart under a microscope.
comments: They are one of the only non-primates with them at all.
For anyone who likes a genuinely useless coincidence → https://beastlyfacts.com/facts/fingerprints-like-ours/

posts.text: Sphynx cats run a higher body temperature and faster metabolism than furred cats, because there is no coat doing the insulating.
comments: Which is why they hunt down warm laps and sunny windowsills, and often need a sweater in winter.
Send it to whoever thinks hairless means low maintenance → https://beastlyfacts.com/facts/always-running-warm/

posts.text: White's tree frogs are hardy for an amphibian, and they have one health issue that shows up here more than in almost any other pet frog, driven by the same enthusiasm that makes them fun to keep.
comments: Obesity is the defining risk. Fat deposits build visibly over the eardrum and in the armpits, and sustained obesity is not cosmetic → https://beastlyfacts.com/blog/whites-tree-frog-health-issues-guide/

posts.text: Red pandas grip bamboo with a false thumb, an extended wrist bone. Giant pandas evolved the identical fix independently.
comments: Two animals that are not close relatives, landing on the same answer.
For anyone who likes convergent evolution → https://beastlyfacts.com/facts/a-thumb-that-isnt-a-thumb/

posts.text: A vulture's stomach acid sits near pH zero, corrosive enough to destroy anthrax and botulism before they reach the bloodstream.
comments: It is effectively a built-in hazmat suit for eating roadkill.
Send it to whoever is squeamish about scavengers → https://beastlyfacts.com/facts/stomach-acid-that-kills-anthrax/

posts.text: Ball pythons are hardy and also sensitive to husbandry mistakes in specific, predictable ways. Most of the list traces back to temperature, humidity, or hygiene.
comments: Respiratory infection is the signature one, and vets see a seasonal spike each winter as enclosures cool down → https://beastlyfacts.com/blog/ball-python-health-issues-guide/

posts.text: A well fed vampire bat brings up blood to feed a hungry roost-mate, but usually only one that has shared with it before.
comments: Skip your turn and the colony remembers.
For anyone who thinks reciprocity is a human invention → https://beastlyfacts.com/facts/bloody-generous/

posts.text: On a moonless night a dung beetle looks up, takes a mental snapshot of the Milky Way, and rolls in a straight line by it.
comments: The only insect known to navigate by the galaxy.
Send it to whoever underestimates insects → https://beastlyfacts.com/facts/steered-by-the-milky-way/

posts.text: A pet mouse is one of the cheapest animals to buy and one of the easiest to under-budget for, because two facts change the math more than the sticker price does.
comments: Mice have to live in a group rather than alone, and most fancy mice run $5 to $10 from a breeder. The group is the part people miss → https://beastlyfacts.com/blog/mouse-cost-guide/

posts.text: Some glass frogs are transparent enough underneath that you can watch the heart beating through the skin.
comments: Asleep, they pack nearly all their red blood cells into the liver, which makes them harder to spot on a leaf.
For anyone who likes a genuinely see-through animal → https://beastlyfacts.com/facts/see-through-bellies/

posts.text: A secretary bird hunts venomous snakes on foot, kicking with five times its own body weight and resetting in a fraction of a second.
comments: The absurd legs keep the body out of biting range while the stomping happens.
Send it to someone who thinks birds avoid danger → https://beastlyfacts.com/facts/the-snake-stomping-kickboxer/

posts.text: California kingsnakes are hardy, and the overwhelming majority of health problems in this species come from husbandry errors rather than any fragility in the animal.
comments: Wheezing, open-mouth breathing, nasal mucus and lethargy point to respiratory infection, from temperatures too low, excess humidity, or poor hygiene → https://beastlyfacts.com/blog/california-kingsnake-health-issues-guide/

posts.text: Male gharials grow a bulbous knob on the tip of the snout and use it to blow bubbles and buzz underwater at females.
comments: The needle-thin jaws are built purely for fish. Too fragile for anything bigger.
For whoever has never heard of this crocodilian → https://beastlyfacts.com/facts/the-nose-knows-best/

posts.text: The USDA's Beagle Brigade has been sniffing out smuggled fruit, meat, and plants in airport luggage since 1984, from one dog to around 120.
comments: Beagles got the job partly because nobody is frightened of a beagle.
Send it to anyone who has been stopped by one → https://beastlyfacts.com/facts/the-usdas-nose-squad/

posts.text: Red-eared sliders are sold cheap and small, which is exactly what makes the real cost easy to underestimate. The animal is inexpensive. What it grows into is not.
comments: Hatchlings run $10 to $40, most listings $15 to $30. The 100-plus gallon enclosure is the number nobody quotes at the counter → https://beastlyfacts.com/blog/red-eared-slider-cost-guide/

posts.text: Slow lorises lick a gland on the inside of the elbow, mix the secretion into their saliva, and bite. The only venomous primate.
comments: That bite can put a person into anaphylactic shock.
For whoever has watched the tickling videos → https://beastlyfacts.com/facts/the-only-venomous-primate/

posts.text: A kiwi egg can weigh a fifth of the mother's body weight. An ostrich egg is about 2 percent of hers.
comments: Kiwis are also the only birds with nostrils at the tip of the beak, for sniffing out grubs underground.
Send it to whoever thinks ostriches win the egg category → https://beastlyfacts.com/facts/the-impossible-egg/

posts.text: Madagascar hissing cockroaches are the most affordable pet on this entire site, to buy and to keep. That is not a joke entry, it is the actual answer.
comments: Nymphs run about $3 each, a breeding pair about $24, a starter colony of 25 around $65 → https://beastlyfacts.com/blog/madagascar-hissing-cockroach-cost-guide/

posts.text: A greyhound hits 45 mph in a short sprint, the fastest dog alive, and it hunts by sight rather than scent.
comments: Which is why a retired racer will ignore a scent trail and lock onto a plastic bag moving across a field.
For anyone considering adopting one → https://beastlyfacts.com/facts/the-sprinting-specialist/

posts.text: Sawfish are not sharks. They are rays, and the tooth-studded snout is packed with thousands of pores reading other animals' electrical fields.
comments: It finds prey buried in sand without ever seeing it.
Send it to whoever calls them saw sharks → https://beastlyfacts.com/facts/the-living-metal-detector/

posts.text: Ackie monitors are a real step up in investment from most beginner lizards, both in what the animal costs and in what housing one properly takes.
comments: Yellow ackies sit toward the lower end. Red ackies are larger, less common, and command a premium, often $250 to $400 → https://beastlyfacts.com/blog/ackie-monitor-cost-guide/

posts.text: The pronghorn runs close to 55 mph to escape the American cheetah, which went extinct thousands of years ago.
comments: Second fastest land animal alive, still built for a chase that no longer happens.
For anyone who likes evolutionary leftovers → https://beastlyfacts.com/facts/built-to-outrun-a-ghost/

posts.text: Coconut crab claws have been measured pinching at over 3,000 newtons, in the range of a lion's bite.
comments: Largest land arthropod alive, and yes, it opens coconuts with that.
Send it to whoever is scared of the spider in the bathroom → https://beastlyfacts.com/facts/grip-like-a-lions-bite/

posts.text: Cherry shrimp are cheap to buy, and the real budgeting question is not the price tag. It is how fast a starting group of ten becomes a colony of fifty without you doing anything.
comments: They are graded on how solid and opaque the red is, and price climbs with grade → https://beastlyfacts.com/blog/cherry-shrimp-cost-guide/

posts.text: A protein from Gila monster venom, exendin-4, became the basis for early diabetes drugs and helped inspire the GLP-1 medications behind Ozempic.
comments: It is also the only venomous lizard native to the US, living off tail fat between a few meals a year.
For anyone who thinks venom research is a dead end → https://beastlyfacts.com/facts/from-venom-to-ozempic/
